paragraphs: Scientific annotation involves more than producing a final label: experts explore data, check suggestions, and repair mistakes. This paper studies whether models can learn those working habits through behavioral cloning. It introduces nine synthetic tasks with simulated annotation behavior, providing a controlled setting for examining how models acquire the steps involved in scientific annotation.

The experiments suggest that these skills develop in stages. Models learn interface mechanics before learning the decisions that determine task success. They also make fewer mistakes than their demonstrations while retaining the ability to correct errors. Within the tested scale range, larger models use training data more efficiently, and training across multiple tasks enables adaptation to new tasks where training from scratch fails.

The authors also examine internal representations using linear probes. They find information about task phase, data position, and a mistake representation shared across tasks. These findings establish a basis for studying annotation workflows as learnable behavior, while the evidence itself comes from synthetic tasks designed to support eventual work on real scientific annotation.
icml-2026-a-systematic-study-of-behavior.tldr: Models trained on synthetic annotation workflows learn interface skills, correction behavior, and transferable task representations.

paragraphs: Generative models often learn by making one probability distribution resemble another, but their training procedures can look quite different. This paper develops Generative Wasserstein Flows, a theoretical framework that places many such procedures within a common account of optimization over distributions. Its starting point is a continuous evolution described by Wasserstein gradient flows.

The connection to practical algorithms comes through the Jordan–Kinderlehrer–Otto scheme, which turns that continuous evolution into discrete optimization steps. The authors show that a broad class of existing methods follows from parameterized versions of this scheme for objectives based on f-divergences. They also establish equivalences between several recent algorithms, explaining how apparently different constructions can share the same underlying formulation.

The framework extends to Integral Probability Metrics and squared Maximum Mean Discrepancy, yielding additional generative algorithms and clarifying relationships with GANs. The paper empirically studies JKO regularization across objectives and analyzes flows restricted to distributions generated by parameterized maps. Its contribution is both organizational and constructive: it connects existing approaches while providing a route to new ones.
icml-2026-a-unifying-view-of-variational.tldr: A Wasserstein-flow framework connects existing generative algorithms and derives new ones through a shared optimization scheme.

paragraphs: LoRA fine-tunes a model through pairs of low-rank factors that together define a weight update. Different factor pairs can produce exactly the same adapted weight matrix. This paper shows that this redundancy matters for optimization: mathematically equivalent updates can have substantially different condition numbers, which describe how difficult the surrounding optimization problem is to navigate.

The authors establish this effect theoretically and empirically, linking the particular loss minimizer reached in factor space to convergence speed. Their proposed method, Balanced Low-Rank Adaptation, periodically projects the factors onto a balanced manifold. The projection preserves the adapted matrix while improving the conditioning of the loss landscape, changing the optimization representation without changing the matrix represented at that step.

The projection is described as lightweight and compatible with existing fine-tuning pipelines. Across the reported tasks, BaLoRA converges faster and performs better than standard LoRA. The broader finding is that optimization can improve by choosing better representatives among equivalent parameter settings, making the structure of LoRA's factorization a useful target for accelerating fine-tuning.
icml-2026-balanced-lora-removing-paramet.tldr: BaLoRA balances equivalent low-rank factors to improve optimization conditioning and empirically accelerate fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Stochastic optimization must cope with errors in gradient estimates, and heavy-tailed errors can include exceptionally large disturbances. This paper asks whether stochastic mirror descent retains convergence guarantees when those errors can have infinite variance. It develops a continuous-time model driven by centered Lévy noise with a finite p-th moment, for p greater than one and at most two.

The resulting Lévy mirror flow arises as a scaling limit of stochastic mirror descent. When p is below two, its paths can have jumps of arbitrary size; sufficiently frequent jumps can produce infinite variance. Despite this behavior, the authors prove bounds on the time required to reach a prescribed level of optimization accuracy for convex and relatively strongly convex objectives.

For error tolerance epsilon, the bounds scale as epsilon to the power minus p divided by p minus one in the convex case, and minus one divided by p minus one, up to logarithmic factors, under relative strong convexity. Matching discrete-time guarantees extend the analysis to several mirror-descent variants, quantifying how heavier noise changes convergence.
icml-2026-bregman-meets-levy-stochastic-.tldr: Mirror descent can retain quantified convergence guarantees under heavy-tailed noise, including noise with infinite variance.

paragraphs: Sampling becomes difficult when a target distribution has several separated regions of high probability and evaluating its density is expensive. Conditional Diffusion Sampling combines two ways of approaching this problem: Parallel Tempering for exploration and diffusion-based transport for moving samples toward the target. The aim is to use density evaluations more effectively without training a neural transport model.

The mathematical ingredient is a family of Conditional Interpolants whose transport follows an exact, closed-form stochastic differential equation. These processes require samples from a challenging initialization distribution. The authors show theoretically and empirically that obtaining this initialization becomes less costly when diffusion times are sufficiently short, giving a concrete condition under which the construction becomes attractive.

The algorithm therefore first uses Parallel Tempering to sample the initialization and then transports those samples through the derived dynamics. This assigns global exploration and local movement to complementary procedures. Experiments suggest the combination could offer a better trade-off between sample quality and density-evaluation cost than leading samplers; the abstract presents this as potential supported by experiments.
icml-2026-conditional-diffusion-sampling.tldr: Conditional Diffusion Sampling combines Parallel Tempering with exact diffusion transport to potentially improve sampling efficiency without neural training.

paragraphs: A learning system that releases models throughout training must protect privacy across the entire sequence of releases. This paper studies participation privacy when neighboring user streams differ by one insertion or deletion. Such an edit shifts subsequent updates, making standard analyses based on changing a fixed stream position insufficient for this setting.

The proposed recipe first places incoming updates into randomized buffers containing between U and twice U items. This converts the stream comparison into a form that standard per-bin privacy mechanisms can handle, with explicit guarantees on backlog and delay. The buffer scale U is chosen using the desired privacy parameters, directly connecting privacy protection with waiting time.

A second result lifts non-adaptive privacy proofs to adaptive inputs for mechanisms satisfying the stated decomposition, prefix-causality, and fresh-noise conditions. Together, these components give differential privacy for the full release trajectory under single-edit stream changes using standard primitives such as tree prefix sums. Streaming DP-SGD experiments examine the resulting utility, privacy, latency, and delay distributions.
icml-2026-continual-learning-with-partic.tldr: Randomized buffering and a conditional certification theorem provide participation privacy across adaptively released learning trajectories.

paragraphs: Diffusion guidance steers generated samples toward requested conditions. A common way to exclude unwanted content is to negate the usual classifier-free guidance term. This paper identifies a problem with that approach: reversing the guidance creates an inverted probability distribution that can push samples away from the model's marginal distribution and distort their appearance.

ContrastiveCFG instead derives guidance from a contrastive loss. Depending on whether a concept is wanted or unwanted, the loss aligns the denoising direction with the condition or repels it. This gives positive conditions a guiding effect similar to standard classifier-free guidance while addressing the stated shortcomings of applying a simple sign reversal for negative conditions.

Experiments show that the method can introduce or remove concepts while preserving sample quality across the tested scenarios. These range from simple class conditions to complex text prompts with overlapping concepts. The contribution is a sampling-time mechanism for handling attraction and avoidance through the same contrastive formulation, with empirical evidence that concept control and sample quality can coexist.
icml-2026-contrastivecfg-guiding-diffusi.tldr: ContrastiveCFG uses contrastive guidance to add or suppress diffusion concepts while maintaining sample quality in reported experiments.

paragraphs: This paper trains language models to answer open-ended questions about future events. To obtain training examples at scale, the authors generate forecasting questions from daily global news. A central finding is that directly using the generated data hurts performance, whereas carefully selecting questions produces the useful OpenForesight training dataset.

The authors use this dataset to post-train Qwen3 thinking models. Both question generation and information retrieval rely on an offline news collection to prevent future information from leaking into training or evaluation. A small validation set guides the use of retrieval and an improved reinforcement-learning reward function, connecting data curation with the design of the forecasting system.

In held-out testing, OpenForecaster-8B matches much larger proprietary models. The reported training gains cover accuracy, calibration, and consistency: predictions improve, confidence better reflects correctness, and answers become more consistent. Calibration gains also transfer across popular benchmarks. The results support a recipe in which careful question selection, controlled information access, and forecasting-specific training jointly improve performance.
icml-2026-curating-the-future-a-scalable.tldr: Curated news-derived questions and forecasting-specific training produce an 8B model that matches much larger proprietary forecasters in held-out testing.

paragraphs: Scientific reasoning needs evaluation of intermediate steps as well as final answers. Process Reward Models provide that finer supervision, but expert checking of every step is expensive. This paper addresses how to train reliable process evaluators from abundant, noisy labels supplied by weaker supervisors, with biological reasoning as its stated application.

DC-W2S judges supervision using two forms of agreement. Self-Consensus measures agreement among weak supervisors, while Neighborhood-Consensus measures agreement in the embedding space. Combining these signals separates training supervision into different reliability regimes. The method then uses a curriculum with balanced sampling of examples and reliability-aware masking of labels to determine how that supervision influences training.

The reported results show that this selection strategy can train robust process reward models without exhaustive expert annotation. The authors find strategic curation more effective than indiscriminately training on large noisy datasets. The contribution is therefore an operational approach to weak-to-strong training: agreement signals guide which examples and labels receive attention, making supervision quality a central part of the learning procedure.
icml-2026-dc-w2s-dual-consensus-weak-to-.tldr: DC-W2S combines two agreement signals to curate noisy supervision for reliable step-by-step biological reasoning evaluators.

paragraphs: State-space models describe observations through underlying states that are not directly observed. When observations arrive sequentially, learning must continually update both the model and its account of those hidden states. This paper introduces an online variational procedure that efficiently computes the evidence lower bound, a training objective, together with its gradient in this streaming setting.

The algorithm combines independent, identically distributed Monte Carlo samples with a deliberately chosen deep architecture. This supports simultaneous learning of model parameters and the distribution of latent states conditioned on observations. Its design aims to combine computational efficiency with flexibility, addressing the two linked estimation problems within the same procedure as new data arrive.

The authors illustrate performance on synthetic observations and real air-quality data. Their theoretical motivation rests on an asymptotic contrast function and ergodicity of the underlying Markov chain. They also identify a broader use beyond the particular training objective: computing posterior expectations of additive quantities in state-space models. The contribution thus covers both streaming learning and a related class of posterior calculations.
icml-2026-efficient-online-variational-e.tldr: An online Monte Carlo procedure jointly learns state-space model parameters and latent-state distributions from streaming observations.

paragraphs: Combining several preference lists into one ranking can leave some groups underrepresented, particularly among the candidates who receive attention or selection. This paper studies aggregation with explicit group-representation constraints. It measures disagreement using Spearman footrule distance, which adds up absolute differences in candidates' ranking positions.

The first problem asks for a fair aggregate top-k list, reflecting settings where only the highest-ranked candidates matter. The authors provide the first optimal algorithm for this formulation. The second problem asks for a fair ranking of all candidates. For that setting, they improve the known approximation factor from three to two, tightening the worst-case guarantee on the aggregation objective relative to an optimal fair solution.

These results distinguish two computational outcomes: exact optimization for the top-k problem and a stronger approximation for full ranking. Experiments on real datasets corroborate the theoretical results and show strong performance against existing methods. The work advances the computational treatment of the specified fairness constraints while retaining an explicit measure of agreement with the input preferences.
icml-2026-fairness-in-aggregation-optima.tldr: The paper gives an optimal fair top-k aggregation algorithm and improves fair full-ranking approximation from a factor of three to two.

paragraphs: Coding assistants increasingly receive visual designs alongside written instructions, so generating useful code requires interpreting diagrams as well as text. This paper addresses the shortage of training data and evaluation resources for that workflow across programming languages. It introduces a coordinated set of resources for learning and testing code generation from visual inputs.

The training dataset, M²C-INSTRUCT, contains more than 13.1 million examples spanning over 50 programming languages. The authors use it to train M²-CODER, a multimodal software-development model that combines visual designs with textual requests. They also introduce M²EVAL, a multilingual benchmark intended to assess code generation when visual understanding forms part of the task.

In the reported experiments, the seven-billion-parameter M²-CODER performs comparably to models with more than 70 billion parameters. This result supports the effectiveness of the supplied training data for the evaluated tasks. Together, the dataset, model, and benchmark make the contribution broader than a single coding system: they provide resources for training and measuring assistants that translate visual design into programs.
icml-2026-from-diagrams-to-code-multilin.tldr: A large multilingual diagram-to-code dataset supports a 7B coding model that matches much larger models in reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning for code generation often concentrates on Python, with weaker transfer to other programming languages. Training separately across several languages can also produce uneven optimization and fail to pass useful knowledge from languages with abundant resources to those with fewer. GXPO addresses this imbalance by connecting training examples through the programming problem they solve.

For each problem, GXPO generates solutions in multiple programming languages and puts them into a shared training group. Optimization then incorporates both signals specific to each language and signals spanning languages. This grouping makes the relationship among alternative implementations part of the training procedure, supporting more balanced learning and transfer to languages with less available training support.

The authors also introduce Multilingual LiveCodeBench, extending LiveCodeBench into a unified multilingual evaluation setting. Across eight programming languages on this benchmark, GXPO consistently improves performance, with especially pronounced gains for lower-resource languages. The results support jointly organized multilingual reinforcement learning as a way to improve code generation across languages while preserving attention to each language's requirements.
icml-2026-gxpo-group-cross-lingual-relat.tldr: GXPO groups multilingual solutions to the same problem during reinforcement learning, improving code generation especially in lower-resource languages.

paragraphs: Self-speculative decoding speeds up generation by using a reduced version of a language model to draft tokens. Selecting which layers to skip creates a trade-off between drafting cost and how faithfully the draft matches the full model. KnapSpec addresses the fact that this trade-off changes with context length and hardware, particularly as attention becomes more expensive.

The method treats draft selection as a knapsack optimization problem aimed at maximizing tokens generated per unit time. It considers attention and MLP layers separately, models their hardware-specific latency as context length changes, and uses parallel dynamic programming to adapt the draft configuration. A theoretical analysis supports cosine similarity between hidden states as a proxy for token acceptance.

Experiments on Qwen3 and Llama3 report consistent improvements over leading self-speculative decoding methods, with wall-clock speedups reaching 1.47 times. KnapSpec requires no additional training and preserves the target model's output distribution. Its contribution is an adaptive selection procedure that balances draft faithfulness against changing computation costs during long-sequence inference.
icml-2026-knapspec-self-speculative-deco.tldr: KnapSpec adapts speculative draft layers to context length and hardware, achieving reported speedups up to 1.47 times without extra training.

paragraphs: Medical vision-language systems need to connect what they say about an image with the regions they identify inside it. MedSIGHT addresses the difficulty of combining image comprehension and segmentation in one framework. Its goal is to give language-based interpretation a structured connection to anatomical and pathological regions at the pixel level.

A Region Perceiver creates tokens centered on image regions, placing spatial information into representations the language model can use. A medical region codebook adds discrete region symbols to the model's vocabulary. The model can generate these codes, and the Region Perceiver decodes them into segmentation masks, linking symbolic output to a spatial delineation of the image.

The authors combine the language model, codebook, and Region Perceiver through progressive training intended to align the modules stably. Training uses 72,000 multimodal instruction pairs. The reported evaluations achieve state-of-the-art results on both medical comprehension and segmentation across diverse imaging modalities. These findings support the proposed connection between language representations and explicit region outputs within a unified model.
icml-2026-medsight-towards-grounded-visu.tldr: MedSIGHT links medical language understanding to pixel-level segmentation through region tokens, a region codebook, and progressive training.

paragraphs: A mobile robot must choose where to position its base before manipulating an object. Physical reachability alone does not determine whether a learned manipulation policy will succeed, because the policy can be sensitive to its starting arrangement. N2M treats base positioning as a decision that should account for the manipulation policy's preferences.

The method builds on the idea that these preferences are tied to local scene structure and can be learned from policy rollouts. It introduces viewpoint augmentation to learn pose preferences that remain robust across viewing directions. This provides a data-efficient route to learning suitable base positions while addressing the reliance on pre-built scene reconstructions and slow inference identified in earlier approaches.

The reported experiments achieve state-of-the-art performance and outperform both methods that ignore policy preferences and recent methods that incorporate them. Additional analyses examine applicability, generalization, and data efficiency. The main implication is that navigation can be better connected to manipulation by learning where a particular policy works well, using its own executions as evidence.
icml-2026-n2m-bridging-navigation-and-ma.tldr: N2M learns manipulation-policy pose preferences from rollouts to choose better mobile-robot base positions.

paragraphs: A language model labeling content may bring its own understanding of a concept, even when instructions supply a different definition. This paper studies that interaction in toxicity annotation. It introduces Definition-Specific Familiarity, which measures how closely a model's elicited concept matches the definition the annotation task actually requires.

Across nine models and five datasets, this measure predicts annotation performance after accounting for dataset identity, with a partial correlation of positive 0.41. The association stays positive across six prompting conditions. Three common text-memorization measures show no positive association, suggesting that familiarity with the relevant definition is more informative here than those measures of familiarity with text.

Additional instructions or examples correct only 34.8% of initial zero-shot errors, and high-confidence mistakes are especially persistent. Misaligned definitions also systematically shift predictions without lowering reported confidence. These findings support checking whether a model's understanding fits the intended annotation policy when selecting it. In the studied settings, stronger prompting and confident answers do not substitute for validating that fit.
icml-2026-on-the-limits-of-llm-adaptabil.tldr: Toxicity annotation depends on alignment with task definitions, while additional prompting often leaves confident mistakes uncorrected.

paragraphs: Generalized Category Discovery uses labeled examples from known categories to identify both familiar and previously unseen categories in unlabeled images. This paper argues that whole-image representations and category labels can overlook the detailed visual evidence needed to distinguish closely related categories. PartCo adds correspondences between image parts to the discovery process.

These correspondences connect local visual features across examples, giving the model information about finer semantic structure. The approach therefore incorporates how visual parts relate, alongside the broader information already used by category-discovery methods. PartCo is designed to integrate with existing methods without requiring substantial changes, making it an addition to established approaches.

Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show significant improvements to existing category-discovery approaches, with PartCo outperforming most methods considered. The findings support the value of part-level information when discovering categories, particularly where global descriptions alone miss useful distinctions. The contribution is a way to connect semantic category supervision with detailed visual composition while retaining compatibility with current discovery frameworks.
icml-2026-partco-part-level-corresponden.tldr: PartCo improves discovery of known and novel image categories by adding correspondences between visual parts.

paragraphs: Regression on a constrained domain must account for the domain's structure. Bayesian additive spanning trees address this by dividing spanning-tree components into contiguous regions. However, their hard partitions make smoothly varying relationships difficult to represent. PR-BAST relaxes those boundaries through probabilistic routing along the spanning trees.

The resulting regression surface combines multiple smooth components aligned with the tree structure. Conditional on a fixed spanning tree, each component defines a Gaussian random field with a sparse, tree-structured precision matrix. This mathematical structure supports scalable posterior computation using sparse linear algebra, linking the smoother representation to an efficient computational approach.

The authors prove that PR-BAST has strictly faster posterior contraction than BAST when the true function is smooth on the graph. This guarantee is explicitly tied to that smoothness condition. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets also show improved accuracy over BAST and other baselines while preserving tree-based interpretability. The method thus combines structure-respecting regression with smoother predictions and favorable theoretical behavior for graph-smooth targets.
icml-2026-probabilistically-routed-bayes.tldr: PR-BAST replaces hard spanning-tree partitions with probabilistic routing, improving regression and posterior contraction under graph-smooth truth.

paragraphs: Constrained optimization can become expensive when projecting onto the full feasible region is difficult. This paper studies feasible regions defined by intersecting lower-level sets of convex functions. Its algorithm combines objective-reducing gradient or subgradient steps with randomized feasibility updates, sampling a random number of constraints per iteration and using Polyak steps.

The guarantees depend on the objective. For strongly convex objectives with Lipschitz-smooth gradients, an adaptive step size gives linear convergence in expectation to any prescribed tolerance. For convex objectives that may be nonsmooth, a fully parameter-free adaptive scheme achieves an expected worst-case rate proportional to one over the square root of the iteration count.

Constraint violation decreases geometrically with the number of feasibility updates almost surely. The analysis also connects bounds for averaged iterates to the distribution governing how many constraints are sampled, with optimal rates under certain sample-size growth choices. Simulations involving quadratic constraints, support vector machines, and fairness-constrained logistic regression demonstrate computational efficiency relative to existing methods.
icml-2026-randomized-feasibility-methods.tldr: Adaptive optimization with randomized constraint updates provides convergence guarantees without requiring easy projection onto the full feasible region.

paragraphs: Removing a concept from a diffusion model is difficult when that concept is spread across many internal features. SAEmnesia addresses this feature-splitting problem with supervised sparse autoencoders. During training, concept labels encourage a one-to-one mapping between concepts and neurons, concentrating each concept into an interpretable feature that can be targeted for erasure.

This centralization simplifies the intervention: the method can act on a dedicated neuron instead of searching across many distributed features. Compared with the stated leading sparse-autoencoder unlearning approach, SAEmnesia reduces hyperparameter search by 96.67% and improves the object result on UnlearnCanvas by 9.22%. These findings connect the representation design with both reduced tuning effort and better benchmark performance.

The paper also examines sequential removal of multiple concepts, reporting a 28.4% accuracy improvement when removing nine objects. Additional evaluations show nudity suppression on I2P and robustness to adversarial attacks. Together, the reported results support supervised feature organization as a way to make concept erasure more precise and scalable across the tested settings.
icml-2026-saemnesia-erasing-concepts-in-.tldr: SAEmnesia concentrates concepts into individual sparse-autoencoder neurons to make diffusion-model concept erasure more targeted and efficient.

paragraphs: Training web agents directly on real websites creates practical difficulties: exploration can have unwanted consequences, sites are hard to reset, and success is often difficult to verify. VeriEnv uses language models to recreate real websites as executable synthetic environments. This gives agents places to practice while separating their training interactions from live websites.

The recreated environments expose controlled internal access through a Python SDK. Agents use this access to generate tasks whose outcomes can be checked deterministically by programs. That design supplies verifiable rewards without relying on heuristic scoring or language-model judges, making task generation and feedback part of the same environment-building framework.

Experiments on web-agent benchmarks show that agents trained with VeriEnv can generalize to unseen websites. They also develop site-specific mastery through self-evolving training and improve as the number of training environments increases. The findings support environment creation as a scalable component of agent learning: expanding the collection of executable websites provides additional opportunities for practice with directly checkable outcomes.
icml-2026-safe-and-scalable-web-agent-le.tldr: VeriEnv trains web agents on recreated websites with programmatically verified rewards, supporting transfer and scalable practice.

paragraphs: Large language models devote much of their parameter count and computation to feedforward layers. This paper targets those costs using unstructured sparsity, where many individual entries can be zero without following a fixed block pattern. The work combines a study of how much sparsity models tolerate with GPU machinery designed to make that sparsity computationally useful.

The authors introduce a sparse packing format and CUDA kernels that fit into optimized modern GPU execution pipelines. These support sparse computation during both training and inference. Their quantitative study finds that simple L1 regularization can induce more than 99% sparsity with negligible effects on downstream performance in the reported setting.

When paired with the proposed kernels, these sparse models show substantial improvements in throughput, energy efficiency, and memory use. The benefits increase with model scale. The result connects two necessary pieces of the proposed efficiency strategy: learning highly sparse feedforward layers while retaining performance, and executing those layers efficiently enough for the sparsity to deliver practical resource savings.
icml-2026-sparser-faster-lighter-transfo.tldr: Highly sparse feedforward layers and specialized GPU kernels deliver reported language-model speed, energy, and memory benefits with negligible performance impact.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning can change a language model's behavior beyond the examples it was trained on, sometimes in unwanted ways. Concept Ablation Fine-Tuning addresses this by intervening in the model's internal representations during training. It aims to steer generalization without changing the fine-tuning examples or using data from the target distribution.

CAFT starts with latent-space directions corresponding to undesirable concepts, identified through interpretability tools. During fine-tuning, linear projections ablate these directions. This gives the training procedure a way to suppress particular concepts while retaining the original data, making the availability of suitable concept directions central to the method.

The authors successfully apply CAFT to three tasks, including emergent misalignment, where narrow fine-tuning produces severely misaligned responses to broader questions. They report a tenfold reduction in misaligned responses without degraded performance on the training distribution. These results show that, in the tested tasks, changing which internal concepts are available during learning can influence how the model generalizes while preserving its performance on the fine-tuning distribution.
icml-2026-steering-out-of-distribution-g.tldr: CAFT ablates undesirable internal concept directions during fine-tuning, reducing reported misaligned responses tenfold without changing training data.

paragraphs: Model-based reinforcement learning uses predictions to help choose actions, but this paper finds that adding search does not automatically improve a learned policy. Search can reduce performance even when the predictive model is highly accurate. This challenges the view that inaccurate long-term predictions and accumulated model errors are the main barriers to effective search.

The authors instead identify overestimation bias as a more consequential issue in their investigation. Improving model or value-function accuracy matters less than controlling overly optimistic value estimates. Their proposed response uses an ensemble of value functions and takes the minimum estimate, introducing a conservative evaluation into the search procedure.

With this change, search becomes effective and achieves state-of-the-art performance across several popular benchmark domains. The findings shift attention from predictive accuracy alone to how values are used when comparing possible actions. They show that a highly accurate model can still support poor search decisions, while addressing optimistic valuation can make search beneficial in the evaluated settings.
icml-2026-the-surprising-difficulty-of-s.tldr: Search can hurt even with accurate models; taking minimum ensemble values controls overestimation and enables strong benchmark performance.
